name: Ecuador
sources: GDP $15.2bn and 10.5m people (World Bank NY.GDP.MKTP.CD and SP.POP.TOTL, 1990; exact prints $15.239bn and 10,473,673). CORRECTION WORTH RECORDING: this row first carried $10.6bn, which is not any World Bank print for Ecuador in any year near 1990 and would have implied output per head of about $1,010 against a real figure near $1,455. It was caught by querying the series directly rather than by any test, because no test in this repo can tell a plausible wrong number from a right one - which is the argument for the sources block existing at all.

Inflation 48.5% is the Banco Central del Ecuador CPI annual average for 1990 (December-on-December 49.5%), sustained by the crawling-peg devaluation of the sucre. interest_rate 52% is the commercial lending benchmark after the 1986 liberalisation; the sucre loses roughly a third of its dollar value across the year.
Tax take 15% of GDP, most of it oil rent remitted by CEPE (Petroecuador from 1989); non-oil revenue was under 10% of GDP.

Debt 0.72: external debt about $12.1bn at end-1990 (World Bank), roughly 79% of GDP, of which the public share is around $10.9bn - 72% of GDP, which is the figure this row carries. This ratio was recomputed after the GDP correction above; at the wrong GDP it read 1.00 and made Ecuador the most indebted state in the region, which it was not. Ecuador had suspended commercial interest payments in 1987 after the March earthquake broke the trans-Andean pipeline and cut oil exports for five months, and stayed in arrears until the 1994 Brady deal.
Oil 0.29 mbd: about 292,000 bbl/d in 1990. Ecuador left OPEC in 1992 rather than pay the dues and accept the quota.

Defence 1.9% of GDP and strength 4. The binding external fact is the undemarcated Cordillera del Condor frontier with Peru: Ecuador rejected the 1942 Rio Protocol as invalid in 1960, there were shooting incidents at Paquisha in 1981, and the Cenepa war follows in January 1995. That war should be reachable from the border and the relations here, not fired by a date.

Stability 40 and separatism 0.08: Rodrigo Borja's government faced the first national indigenous uprising, the levantamiento of June 1990 organised by CONAIE, which closed the Sierra highways for a week and put land and plurinationality on the agenda permanently. No president elected between 1996 and 2006 finished a term; that instability is the thing this row is trying to seed.
